rv.q: But in the end, it is too cluttered — stylistically, tonally, ideologically — to offer much insight.
Dark Noon is a frenetic, triumphant production that is both hugely entertaining and deeply thought-provoking for American audiences in particular.
As of now, both High Noon and Dark Noon are must-sees, the former as perfect of its kind, the latter flawed but endlessly insistent
If nothing else, it’s one of the most gleefully provocative pieces of theater you’ll see this year.
It’s jaw-droppingly audacious, and breathtakingly fearless, daring you to either look away or challenge what you’re seeing.
